subject: MAP: performance benchmarking, throughput economics, and close timeline (Acme Financial)
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmefin.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@acmefin.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Performance MAP kickoff and initial ask

Soojin / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Acme’s engineering and ops teams are aligned to run a short MAP focussed on production throughput and unit economics so we can finalize procurement by the end of October. High-level asks from our side:

- A concrete benchmarking plan that measures sustained QPS, tokens/sec, and TTFT (time-to-first-token).
- Clear acceptance criteria for latency by percentile (p50/p95) under our target concurrency.
- A short unit-econ summary (cost per 1M tokens and expected monthly cost at our forecast).
- A proposed timeline to close the POC and contract.

Can you send a MAP draft and proposed test harness by EOD Friday? We’ll provide traffic profiles and a small sample of anonymized prompts.

Appreciate it —
Jordan
Ops Lead, Acme Financial

[attachment: sample-prompts-50.txt text/plain]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmefin.com>, Ops Team <ops@acmefin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance MAP kickoff and initial ask

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is a draft MAP and the benchmarking harness spec (attachments: 20261001-map-draft.pdf, bench-harness-spec.md). Key points from the plan below so everyone has a single view:

1) Test objectives
- Validate sustained throughput and unit economics for Acme’s expected workload (median prompt length ~120 tokens, 60% chat-like, 40% transactional).
- Measure TTFT, p50/p95 token latency, and stability over 30–60 minute sustained windows.

2) Workload profile and scenarios- Steady-state sustained run: target steady QPS values {50, 100, 200} for 30 minutes each.
- Burst/recovery: 5x short burst for 60s to measure tail latency and KV cache hit impact.
- Cold-start: instances started from cold, measure TTFT and first few tokens throughput.
- Cache-warm vs cache-cold: run identical sequence with and without prefix caching.

3) Metrics and acceptance criteria- TTFT (time-to-first-token): target p50 < 20ms, p95 < 60ms for dedicated pools.
- Sustained QPS: ability to sustain target QPS with p95 latency < 150ms and p50 < 60ms.
- Tokens/sec: report aggregate tokens/sec and per-GPU throughput.
- Stability: no >1% error rate and <5% throughput variance during sustained window.

4) Unit economics (initial estimate)- Baseline pricing (hosted): $8.50 per 1M tokens (model variant A, standard quant).
- Projected optimized cost (dedicated + quant + batching): ~$2.7 per 1M tokens (assumes 4x batching and prefix caching gains).
- For Acme forecast (10M tokens/day): baseline ~= $85/day (~$2.6k/mo); optimized ~= $27/day (~$800/mo). We’ll validate these numbers after measured tokens/sec and GPU utilization.

5) Test harness and data- We’ll run a replay harness within your VPC (or Redwood dedicated test harness) that preserves timing and concurrency.
- Test data: your anonymized prompts + 10% synthetic edge cases.

6) Timeline / MAP milestones- 2026-10-05: final MAP sign-off and test data delivered by Acme ops.
- 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-11: run initial sweeps at 50/100 QPS.
- 2026-10-12: deep sustained runs at target 200 QPS.
- 2026-10-18: tuning pass (quantization, batching, routing).
- 2026-10-25: final acceptance tests and cost validation.
- 2026-10-28: POC close and contract execution.

If anything in the acceptance criteria looks unrealistic for your environment, flag it and we’ll adjust. I’m copying Marcus and Neha to help with execution.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance MAP kickoff and initial ask

Team —

Quick internal notes on the plan before we run:
- Increase ramping for the 200 QPS run: 5-minute steady ramp rather than 1 minute to avoid generators throttling network stacks.
- Add a KV-cache-degradation scenario (simulate cache miss rate at 30%) — I’ve attached bench-scenarios.csv with scenario params.
- Include a model-variant fallback run (A -> A-quant -> B-small) to verify graceful degradation and unit-econ delta.
- During sustained runs capture GPU p95 utilization and OOM events; if we see memory pressure we’ll flag for a different kernel selection.

I’ll run the harness from our east-us rig and coordinate with Neha for logs collection.

Marcus
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: bench-scenarios.csv text/csv]

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmefin.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@acmefin.com>, Ops Team <ops@acmefin.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance MAP kickoff and initial ask — preliminary run results attached

Soojin —

We completed the first deep sustained runs today (attached acme-bench-1012.csv). Highlights / concerns:

- Target: 200 QPS sustained for 30 minutes. Observed sustained QPS: 165 QPS (tokens/sec aggregated 19,800).
- p95 latency during the steady window: 180ms (above the 150ms threshold). p50 ~ 72ms.
- TTFT: p50 35ms, p95 90ms (cold-starts are higher than expected).
- GPU utilization averaged 62% with spikes to 94% during bursts. No OOMs but memory pressure noted around burst recovery.
- Error rate: 0.4% (transient infra throttles during a 90s window).

Can you help interpret whether the gap to 200 QPS is an infra limit or model/kernel selection? We kept batching conservative (batch size cap = 8) to preserve latency for interactive flows.

Thanks —
Jordan

[attachment: acme-bench-1012.csv text/csv]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmefin.com>, Ops Team <ops@acmefin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance MAP kickoff and initial ask — analysis and revised closure plan

Jordan / Samira —

Thanks for the run and the CSV; useful signal. High-level read and next steps below. I’ll also drop the finalized MAP doc to the shared Drive (link in metadata).

Root-cause diagnosis (initial):
- The shortfall to 200 QPS looks like a combination of conservative client-side batching + kernel choices that are not optimal for the observed sequence lengths. GPU headroom and spikes indicate we can push throughput with tuning.
- TTFT is above target partly due to cold-starts and small-per-request overhead (network & TLS setup) in the harness.
- The transient 0.4% error rate maps to a rate-limiter at the edge during the burst; we can eliminate via token-level quota bump for the test window.

Proposed optimizations (can be executed in the MAP tuning pass 10/13–10/18):
1) Model/quant kernel: run A-quant with int8 paths and an optimized transformer kernel — should improve tokens/sec by ~25–40% in our internal runs for 120-token sequences.
2) Aggressive batching during steady windows (cap 16, adaptive batching for interactive latency): target average batch size ~12 while preserving p95 < 150ms.
3) Prefix/KV caching: enable warm cache for repeated prompts — expected to reduce per-request compute by ~30%.
4) Adjust harness ramp and remove client-side conservative caps for the 200 QPS run (Marcus will coordinate).
5) Edge quota bump for the test window to remove the observed 0.4% transient errors.

Updated cost and acceptance notes
- With quant + batching + caching we project tokens/sec improvement enough to reach ~210 QPS sustained in our tuned experiments. That implies an optimized unit cost near the $2.6–3.0 per 1M tokens range.
- Revised acceptance timeline (MAP milestones):
  - 2026-10-13: apply quant kernel + expanded batching, run targeted 200 QPS sweep.
  - 2026-10-15: KV-cache validation and burst-recovery runs.
  - 2026-10-18: tuning complete, initial acceptance (p95 < 150ms at sustained 200 QPS).
  - 2026-10-25: final verification runs and cost validation.
  - 2026-10-28: POC close / sign.

Commercial offer (quick):
- If Acme signs by 10/28 we’ll extend a 3-month onboarding credit equal to 10% of first-quarter usage (applied as service credits) and a preferred unit price locked for the first 12 months (price to be finalized with sales).

Next steps
- Marcus / I will run the 10/13 sweep from our east-us rig; we’ll request a short quota window and coordinate a 30-minute monitoring call with your ops to watch metrics live.
- Samira, please confirm a 30-minute window on 10/13 morning PT and whether you want the harness inside your VPC or tunneled to Redwood test rig.

I’ll attach the finalized MAP doc after we align on the 10/13 run.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
